subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme-health.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Hi John / Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I misstate anything, please correct.

Key pain points you shared:
- Rising per-token costs and unpredictable billing spikes on OpenAI/Anthropic during peak hours.
- Latency variability for synchronous user-facing flows (avg 350-600ms is too high for some clinical workflows).
- Data residency and audit requirements for PHI-adjacent telemetry (need strong audit logs + KMS integration).
- Concern about dependency risk on a single vendor and limited ability to tune inference cost/latency (batching, quantization).

Current stack / usage:
- Primary inference today: OpenAI chat completions + embeddings for search.
- Volume: ~6M tokens/day, 80% chat, 20% embeddings.
- Some batched background jobs for report generation (non-interactive).
- Devs call OpenAI via server-side API; a subset of infra wants to keep function-calling compatibility.

Success criteria for migration (what success looks like):
1) Equivalent or better response quality for major intents (triage, patient Q&A, admin summaries).
2) <= 1.5x current latency at 95th pct for interactive flows (target: 400ms p95).
3) ~30% reduction in per-token inference cost or similar cost predictability.
4) Auditability: audit logs + KMS/HSM for keys; SOC2 evidence for deployment.
5) Smooth developer transition: API compatibility for chat/function-calling + embeddings.

Model shortlist discussed:
- Llama 3 family (quantization-friendly, strong chat quality)
- Mistral-instruct variants (good cost/quality tradeoff)
- Falcon-40B / 180B variants for heavier NLU tasks (if needed)
- Option to keep an Anthropic/OpenAI adapter for sensitive generation during staged rollout

Compatibility needs:
- Function-calling or structured output support (we map your existing function calls).
- Embeddings API parity and vector store migration guidance.
- Streaming for long-form generation (progressive UI rendering).
- Safety/regeneration hooks and moderation integration to match current guardrails.

Recommended next steps (agreed on call):
1) Technical deep-dive with your engineers (Rishi + Neha to run) — setup a 90-minute session to review request patterns and latency/throughput.
2) Provide a tailored migration PoC: Redwood-hosted test env with Llama 3 + quantized runners, sample cost/latency benchmarks using your sample prompts.
3) Share SOC2 evidence and basic architecture for private deployment options.
4) Align procurement/timeline: you indicated interest in a Dedicated reserved pool if PoC metrics look good.

I attached a short migration plan and our SOC2 snapshot for your security team.

Attachments:
- redwood-migration-plan-v1.pdf (one-pager: POC scope, success metrics, timeline)
- SOC2-snapshot.pdf (controls summary)

Proposed timings:
- Technical deep-dive: Wed 2026-06-24 or Thu 2026-06-25 10:00–11:30 PT
- PoC kick-off: Week of 6/29 (2-week baseline tests)

If that looks right, I'll lock in Rishi & Neha for the deep-dive and send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side:
- Volume may spike to ~10M tokens/day if adoption across two additional workflows goes well. We need autoscaling guidance and burst behavior.
- For quality validation, we'll provide a 200-prompt golden set (intent-level pass/fail + relevance scoring) — want to ensure PoC measures against that.
- On the SOC2 doc: can you confirm retention period for audit logs (we typically require 12 months)?

We're good to do the technical deep-dive on Thu 6/24 at 10 PT — Alice and I will join. Please send calendar invite.

John
Director of Engineering, Acme Health
john.doe@acme-health.com

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic APIs

Great — glad that matches. Quick replies inline:  
- Autoscaling / burst: Redwood Dedicated can provide burst pools and predictable reserved throughput; we'll map expected spike profile in the deep-dive and propose an autoscale policy.
- Golden set: yes, please share the 200-prompt set (we'll run it through Llama 3 / Mistral baseline in PoC and return per-intent metrics).
- Audit log retention: yes, we retain 12 months by default in hosted; Dedicated/Private can be configured for longer retention — Rishi will follow up with specifics.

I've sent a calendar invite for Thu 2026-06-24 10:00–11:30 PT and included a pre-call checklist (sample prompts, traffic profile, key success metrics). Link to shared folder: https://redwood.app/technical-deep-dive/ACME-POC-2026

Next steps for us before the deep-dive:
1) Rishi & Neha will instrument a lightweight benchmark using a small sample of your prompts to estimate latency on a quantized Llama 3 runner.
2) We'll prepare a mapping doc for function-calling parity and embeddings differences.
3) Security: provide detailed SOC2 + KMS integration notes (Rishi).

See you Thursday.

Best,
Marissa

Morning all —

I'll lead the deep-dive and PoC benchmarking. Quick logistics and ask so we can come prepared:  
- Please upload the 200-prompt golden set and a 24-hour traffic sample (anonymized) to the shared folder before Wed EOD.
- Confirm whether function calls include binary blobs or attachments in arguments (impacts streaming).
- We'll provide two baseline configurations for the PoC: (A) Llama 3 quantized 8-bit runner (focus on cost and latency) and (B) Mistral-instruct baseline (focus on quality). If needed we can add Falcon for heavy-NLU intents.

Deliverables from PoC (2 weeks):
- Per-prompt quality scoring against golden set (pass/fail + relevance).
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for interactive and batch flows.
- Cost-per-1M-token estimate for each runner.
- Migration checklist for function-calling and embeddings (dev integration work).

I've attached a short checklist and our SOC2 controls mapping for your security team.
